title: Chapter 1 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of Docker basics, architecture and the hello‑world experience!

questions.question: What real‑world analogy is often used to explain Docker containers?
questions.explanation: Docker containers are like standardised shipping containers – they package an application and its dependencies so it can run anywhere.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of Docker containers?
questions.explanation: Containers do not use a hypervisor; they share the host OS kernel. Hypervisors are used by virtual machines.

questions.question: Docker containers include a full guest operating system like a virtual machine.
questions.explanation: Containers share the host’s OS kernel and do not include a full operating system, making them lightweight.

questions.question: Which component of Docker is responsible for managing images, containers, networks and volumes?
questions.explanation: The Docker daemon (dockerd) is the server process that does all the management work. The client just sends commands.

questions.question: What is a Docker registry?
options: A place to store and share Docker images
A configuration file for Docker daemon
questions.explanation: Docker registries (like Docker Hub) store images. You can pull public images or push your own.

questions.question: The Docker client and Docker daemon must run on the same machine.
questions.explanation: The client can connect to a remote daemon over a network. By default they run locally, but it’s not required.

questions.question: When you run `docker run hello-world` for the first time, what happens if the image is not found locally?
options: The command fails with an error
Docker builds the image from a Dockerfile
Docker pulls the image from a registry
Docker asks you to upload the image
questions.explanation: Docker automatically pulls the image from the configured registry (usually Docker Hub) before creating the container.

questions.question: Which command shows both client and server version information?
questions.explanation: `docker version` displays details about the client (CLI) and the server (daemon).

questions.question: What does the command `docker info` display?
options: System‑wide Docker information like number of containers, storage driver, etc.
The logs of all running containers
questions.explanation: `docker info` provides an overview of the Docker engine’s status and configuration.

questions.question: A Docker image is a read‑only template used to create containers.
questions.explanation: Images are immutable templates. Containers are writable layers on top of an image.

questions.question: Which analogy best describes the relationship between an image and a container?
options: A blueprint and a building built from it
A recipe and the cooked meal
questions.explanation: An image is like a blueprint or recipe; a container is the actual running instance (building or meal) created from it.

questions.question: The command to list all containers (including stopped ones) is `docker ___ -a`.
questions.explanation: `docker ps -a` shows all containers, while `docker ps` only shows running ones.

questions.question: You must install a Linux virtual machine manually before using Docker Desktop on Windows or macOS.
questions.explanation: Docker Desktop includes a lightweight Linux VM automatically, so you don’t need to set it up yourself.

questions.question: Why does a container stop after the hello‑world program finishes?
options: Because Docker limits the run time to 5 seconds
questions.explanation: Docker keeps the container alive only as long as its main process (PID 1) is running. Once it finishes, the container stops.

questions.question: On a Linux system, how can you run Docker commands without `sudo`?
options: Add your user to the `docker` group
questions.explanation: Adding your user to the `docker` group grants permission to access the Docker daemon socket without `sudo`.

questions.question: Which of these is a correct statement about containers vs virtual machines?
options: Containers provide stronger isolation than VMs
questions.explanation: Containers start in milliseconds because they don’t need to boot an entire OS, unlike VMs.

questions.question: You can run Docker containers on Windows and macOS without any Linux component.
questions.explanation: Docker containers rely on Linux kernel features. Docker Desktop includes a hidden Linux VM to provide that kernel.

questions.question: What is Docker Hub?
options: The default public Docker image registry
questions.explanation: Docker Hub is the largest public registry where you can find and share container images.

questions.question: What does the 'Unable to find image 'hello-world:latest' locally' message indicate?
options: The Docker daemon is not running
The image does not exist on Docker Hub
The image is not in the local cache and will be pulled
questions.explanation: This is a normal message when an image hasn’t been downloaded yet. Docker automatically fetches it from the registry.

questions.question: The Docker daemon process is called `______`.
questions.explanation: The daemon binary is named `dockerd`. The client is the `docker` command.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the Docker architecture?
questions.explanation: The typical flow: client sends commands to daemon; daemon pulls/pushes images from/to a registry.

questions.question: Once a Docker image is pulled, it will never need to be downloaded again even if a newer version exists.
questions.explanation: If you explicitly pull or if you run without specifying a tag, Docker may download updates. The local image can become outdated.
